newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-IRABU TO MAKE MAJOR-LEAGUE DEBUT JULY 10 VS DETROIT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-IRABU TO MAKE MAJOR-LEAGUE DEBUT JULY 10 VS DETROIT.

text.p: Japanese pitcher Hideki Irabu will make his Major League Baseball debut with the New York Yankees immediately after the All-Star break, the team announced Thursday.

Irabu will make his major-league debut against the Detroit Tigers at Yankee Stadium on Thursday night, July 10. He is slated to follow that with a second start during the homestand versus the Cleveland Indians on Tuesday afternoon, July 15.
Prior to arriving in New York, Irabu is expected to make two starts for Triple-A Columbus of the International League on June 30 in Rochester and on July 5 in Columbus.

After three outstanding minor-league starts, Irabu was hit hard Wednesday night in a Double-A contest for the Norwich Navigators against the Binghamton Mets in the Double-A Eastern League. yielding five runs and nine hits in five innings. He walked none, struck out four and gave up his first homer.
Irabu signed a four-year, $12.8 million contract with the New York Yankees in late May.

The Yankees sent the San Diego Padres $3 million in cash, outfielder Ruben Rivera and minor-league pitcher Rafael Medina. In addition to Irabu, New York received minor-leaguers Homer Bush, Gordon Amerson and Vernon Maxwell.

The Padres owned the rights to the 28-year-old Irabu as a result of their working agreement with the pitcher's Japanese team, the Chiba Lotte Marines. Irabu was 12-6 and led the Japanese Pacific League with a 2.40 ERA last season.

Irabu will become the fourth Japanese player in the major leagues, joining three other pitchers -- Hideo Nomo of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shigetoshi Hasegawa of the Anaheim Angels and Takashi Kashiwada of the New York Mets.
